summary.headline: Royal Orchid Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 36% YoY to about INR 107 crore, but PAT fell to INR 6.4 crore from INR 10.9 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 36% YoY to about INR 107 crore, with EBITDA up 39% to about INR 33 crore and margin at roughly 30.7% versus 30%. Reported PAT declined to about INR 6.4 crore from INR 10.9 crore, which management attributed to higher finance costs, depreciation and Ind AS effects, and ramp-up of leased properties. On a non-Ind AS basis, management said Q1 FY27 PAT was about INR 9.8 crore versus about INR 12 crore a year earlier. Five managed/franchised hotels with 237 keys were added, contributing negligibly to the quarter; management also flagged about INR 2.5 crore of GST input credit loss from a change in GST treatment and an April-June demand hit from the Middle East flight disruption.

financial_highlights.change: vs about INR 12 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: about INR 2.5 crore in the quarter
financial_highlights.change: company-wide, due to 5% output GST regime

segments.name: JLO hotels (owned, leased, JV)
segments.commentary: Occupancy about 70% and ADR INR 6,233 vs INR 5,488 a year earlier. These hotels account for the bulk of revenue; ICONIQA is the newest asset, opened November 2025.

segments.name: Managed and franchised portfolio
segments.commentary: Occupancy about 60.8% and ADR INR 4,300 vs INR 4,031 a year earlier. Management fee income is the revenue line here; fees grew about 14% last year on 7,700 keys.

segments.name: ICONIQA (single hotel)
segments.commentary: Management said Q1 occupancy was hit by April-June travel disruption (April about 79%, May about 60%, June about 70%) versus about 80% in Feb-March. Breakeven estimated at about INR 85 crore annualised revenue; target INR 100 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management is targeting ROCE of 20%+ within about a year, once ICONIQA stabilises.
Target of INR 100 crore annualised ICONIQA revenue, dependent on Q3 and Q4 performance.
Keys expected to rise from about 7,700 to 11,000+ in the next 24 months; 50+ signed hotels to open over 18-24 months.
Management declined to give a revenue growth rate for the next 2-3 years and said it is not assuring any date for INR 150 crore management fees; Vision 2030 target not specified as revenue or fees.
Keshav Baljee expects employee cost to stabilise within range over about another year as new properties open.
capex_capacity: Added five hotels with 237 keys in Q1 FY27, all managed or franchised, with no capex by the company.
Portfolio about 7,700 keys currently with 11,000+ signed; 50+ hotels signed for opening in next 18-24 months.
Shift toward revenue-share and lease models adds capex and upfront Ind AS cost; management says management contracts carry limited maintenance capex.
Premiumisation plan: about 1,000 five-star keys across owned, leased and JV hotels being upgraded for higher ADR.
Lakshminarayan Palace in Vadodara opened, branded under an ICONIQA collection brand, positioned upper upscale.
demand_pricing: April-June demand hit by flight cancellations linked to the war; management said about 50% of India inbound travel runs through three Middle Eastern carriers, which went to zero.
Business hotels seasonally weakest in Q1 (April-June); management said Q3-Q4 are the strongest quarters.
Leisure destinations performed well while business and airport hotels were hit.
Rain in Mumbai in July and August has weighed on ICONIQA occupancy.
Nearby supply: Fairmont (50 keys), Hilton Garden Inn (170 keys) and Roswin (110 keys) opened around the same time as ICONIQA, adding about 1,000 keys within walking distance.
ICONIQA missed the corporate RFP season, so management is relying on online travel portals and repeat guests.

qa_highlights.question: How much Q1 growth came from the 237 new keys, and what is the growth of the existing base?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jaiswal said the five new hotels are managed/franchised and contributed very negligibly, as only management or franchise fees are earned; growth came from JLO hotels.

qa_highlights.question: What are occupancy and ARR for Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: JLO occupancy about 70% and ADR INR 6,233 (vs INR 5,488). Managed portfolio occupancy 60.8% and ADR INR 4,300 (vs INR 4,031).

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue grow 25% or 30% over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number; managed-segment fees will grow, and JLO growth depends on ICONIQA stabilising over two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: When will profit growth come through, and what is the ex-ICONIQA, ex-Ind AS trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROCE is about 17-18% and targeting 20%+ in about a year. Amit Jaiswal said he was not very happy with ex-ICONIQA performance and cited high tax cost; Arjun Baljee said the hotel is about a year from turning the corner.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ICONIQA's top line decline, and what was occupancy in April-June and August?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jaiswal said April was about 79%, May about 60%, June about 70%; Q4 about 80%. Q1 is seasonally weak and the war hit inbound travel. August occupancy was hit by heavy Mumbai rains.

qa_highlights.question: What is ICONIQA's breakeven and incremental margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven at about INR 85 crore annualised revenue; management said about 60-65% of revenue above that flows to the bottom line, with a target of INR 100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why has employee cost risen from 19-20% to about 23% of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Keshav Baljee cited the new wage code, annual increments, new leases and management team additions; Amit Jaiswal said the average through the year is about 20-23%.

qa_highlights.question: When can the company build a INR 100-150 crore annual management fee business?
qa_highlights.answer: Keshav Baljee said no date is committed for INR 150 crore; fees grew about 14% last year, and the company aims to double fees as quickly as possible.
